thomasjensen:
Generation 1

Thomas Jensen

12.12.1825, Husby — 9.11.1878, at sea

The oldest man we know for certain in the family. Smallholder, fisherman and beach bailiff in Økjær — a holding on land, nets in the sea and an office on the beach. Bought the house in Silkjær in 1854/55; in the deed to the Vedersø land of 1876 he appears as “Thomas Jensen Silkjær” — the earliest known record of the family name, which the newspapers’ death notice later repeated.

Occupation
Smallholder and fisherman in Økjær, Husby parish — and beach bailiff, the parish office for wrecks and stranded goods
Father
Jens Olesen Klit, b. 17 May 1785
Paternal grandfather
Ole Jensen Klit, b. 1753 on Sønder Klit — the family’s roots go back to the middle of the eighteenth century, and the byname then was Klit, not Silkjær
Married
20 November 1853 in Vedersø Church to Anne Marie Jansdatter — the witnesses were the two fathers, and before the wedding he lived with his brother Ole Jensen on Husby Klit [S68]
Brothers and sisters
Among them his brother Ole Jensen, b. 1818; his brother Esper Jensen Klit, 1829—1883, the survivor of the wreck of 1878; and his sister Anne Marie, b. 1837, married to Anders Knudsen Øe, who drowned in the same boat [S69]
Baptised
1 January 1826, Husby Church
Mother
Maren Thomasdatter, b. 4 February 1790 in Stadil
Five children
Niels 1855 · Maren 1857 · Marie 1859 · Kirstine 1860 · Karen Marie 1862
Widower
For fifteen years — from Anne Marie’s death in 1863 to his own in 1878
Died
Lost at sea on 9 November 1878, aged 52, when the boat capsized on the innermost bar off the Stage lifeboat station. Five of six men drowned. Buried in Husby on 17 November
Caveat
He is named among the five dead in Dannevirke 13.11.1878 and Korsør Avis 14.11.1878. The newspapers, written on the day of the disaster, reported that no bodies had drifted ashore; the parish register’s collective note at the burials singles out only Iver Chr. Olesen Kløve’s body as not having come ashore — the other four, Thomas Jensen among them, did.
Chapters
Chapters 1—6 · mentioned again in chapter 9

Sources: S1, S2, S25, S42, S67
annemarie:
Generation 1 · the Tarpgaard family

Anne Marie Jansdatter

25.9.1827, Tarp in Vedersø — 15.8.1863, Økjær

A farmer’s daughter from the neighbouring parish, who married down in land and up in risk. She had barely nine years in Økjær and died at 35, leaving small children. Without her there would have been no Niels — and none of the chapters that follow.

Family
The Tarpgaard family, Tarp in Vedersø parish. Daughter of the farmer Jan Andersen, Tarpgaard
Born
25 September 1827; baptised at home the same day and presented in Vedersø Church on 4 November [S92]
Married
20 November 1853, Vedersø Church
Moved
First to Husby Klit, where the couple lived with Thomas’ brother Ole Jensen; from 1854/55 in their own house in the marsh [S68]
Died
15 August 1863 in Økjær, 35 years old — six weeks before her birthday; the register of deaths writes 36. Buried on 23 August. The column for cause of death is blank, as in several of the parish’s entries that year.
Chapters
Chapters 3—4

Sources: S1, S2, S38, S92
nielsthomsen:
Generation 2 · the man who took the name

Niels Thomsen Silkjær

9.7.1855, Husby — 17.6.1928, Esbjerg Hospital

Smallholder and fisherman in Økjær like his father. In the oldest papers he is simply Niels Thomsen; in the later ones Niels Thomsen Silkjær; the name certificate of 1905 made the name legal, and the parish register of 1920 writes “smallholder Niels Silkjær”. With the farm name the family had, for the first time, a name that could be inherited.

Baptised
22 July 1855, Husby Church
Conscription board
Entered in the levy roll in 1873 (levy district 28, Husby, letter Y, serial no. 5) as Niels Thomsen, son of the smallholder Thomas Jensen — 62¾ inches tall, about 164 cm. The board’s note in 1878: chest measurement 29½ inches, found exempt from military service and struck off the roll. The following year he stood at the lifeboat. [S112]
Married 1)
14 November 1878 — five days after his father’s death and three days before his funeral — to Ane Johanne Kristensen, b. 1843, twelve years older than he. His father stood as witness — the declaration had been made while he was alive. She bore the daughter Ane Marie on 2.3.1880 and died the same year.
Married 2)
10 November 1881 in Husby to Ane Jensen, b. 29.4.1858 in Ejsing near Vinderup
Honoured
The Dannebrogsmænd’s Badge of Honour, awarded on 10 November 1915 as serving boatman — in his thirty-seventh year at the station. He signed the oath of loyalty in Vedersø on 30 November 1915, and his own account of his life lies in the archive of the Chapter of the Royal Orders; after his death the cross was returned on 9 July 1928. The title Dannebrogsmand recurs in Dansk Fiskeristat 1935—36, and the badge is worn visibly in the portrait. [S8, S58, S110, S111]
Occupation 2
Boatman at the Vedersø lifeboat station, appointed on 1 January 1879, retired on grounds of age on 1 October 1916 — 37 years and 9 months. He stands second from the left in the crew photograph, which the archive dates to 1915. [S58]
At the rescues
Took part 7 times with the lifeboat and 8 times with the rocket apparatus in the rescue of 195 shipwrecked people. In his years of service exactly fifteen successful rescue operations are recorded at Vedersø. [S58]
The date
He was appointed 53 days after his father drowned, and 45 days after the burial date in the parish register — at the station whose boat could not put out on 9 November 1878.
Died
17 June 1928 in Esbjerg, buried in Gormsgade Cemetery — in the sources of the time, Esbjerg New Cemetery
Chapters
Chapters 5—8 · mentioned as father and grandfather through to chapter 22

Sources: S1, S2, S8, S15, S58, S110, S111, S112
anejohannek:
Generation 2 · first wife

Ane Johanne Kristensen

25.9.1843, Rindom parish — 13.9.1880, Økjær

She married Niels on 14 November 1878 — five days after his father drowned and three days before his father’s funeral. She was about twelve years older than he, and the marriage lasted less than two years.

Married
14 November 1878, Vedersø Church
Age
She was born in 1843, he in 1855 — she was about twelve years older. Whether the difference in age or the circumstances on the place mattered for the marriage, the sources do not say.
Daughter
Ane Marie, born on 2 March 1880
Died
13 September 1880 in Økjær, 36 years old, just over six months after the birth. Buried in Husby churchyard on 19 September.
Caveat
The marriage entry gives the groom’s father as witness — the declaration was made when the banns were read, so the wedding was being prepared before his death. [S28]

anejensen:
Generation 2 · second wife

Ane Jensen

29.4.1858, Ejsing near Vinderup — 28.6.1936, Esbjerg

She came into a home with a baby after a dead wife and herself bore a large family by dune and marsh. Her last years were spent in a fishing skipper’s home on the harbour in Esbjerg.

Married
10 November 1881, Husby
Nine children
Thomas 1882 · Ane Johanne 1883 · Jens Klaus 1886 · Esper 1888 · Karen Marie 1890 · Ane Kirstine 1892 · Sidsel Kathrine 1894 · Jensine Kristine 1896 · Ellen 1902
Her roots
The parish book points to her parents as Jens Claus and Stine. The family file identifies them as Jens Claus Matzen, b. c. 1831 in Schleswig, and Ane Kirstine Hansdatter of Landtingmark; the full names have not been checked in the Ejsing parish register. The local history account records a schoolboy Jens Claus Mattzen in Husby — examined in arithmetic and discharged from school by the parish board on 15 April 1846, with the booklet’s remark that the foreign-looking spelling was probably owing to his birth and baptism in Angeln in South Schleswig. If the schoolboy is her father — name, parish and age fit — the family’s thread towards the duchies gains both a place and a figure; see caveat 07 [S169]
Died
28 June 1936 at 3 o’clock at Havnegade 179 in Esbjerg — her son Thomas’ address — 78 years old. Buried on 3 July in Gormsgade Cemetery, section Ø, row 11, no. 10, next to her son’s grave. Cause of death: heart failure. The family file has 23 June; the death certificate takes precedence. [S143, S144]
The arc
From Ejsing in 1858 to Esbjerg harbour in 1936: from open boats hauled up on the sand to decked boats with engines
Chapters
Chapters 6 and 8 · mentioned in chapters 11, 14, 19 and 21

Sources: S2, S8, S27, S143, S144, S169
anemarie:
Generation 3 · of the 1st marriage

Ane Marie

2.3.1880 — 26.3.1960, Husby

The eldest of the children, daughter of Niels and his first wife. She passed the name on in the way that came to mark the women of the family: in the middle of her child’s name.

Married
1908 in Husby to the smallholder Ole Lauridsen, b. 29.5.1861 in Husby, of the family the district called “Klem”
Son
Niels Silkjær Lauridsen, b. 9 August 1911 on Husby Klit — his father’s surname last, his mother’s family name in the middle
The son’s life
Smallholder at Damhus, Sønder Nissum, married in 1938 to Elin Kamma Lillelund. Seen at the age of eight in the school photograph from Husby School, 1919.
Eight children
Vort Sogns Historie gives eight [S27]; Margrethe Dorthea 2.9.1908 [S161] · Ane Johanne 1909 · Agnethe 1910 · Niels Silkjær 1911 · Kristine 1913 · Valdemar 1913 · Maren 1915 · Ole 14.5.1916 [S162]
Died
26 March 1960 in Husby, buried there on 31 March — she lived in the parish all her life
Chapters
Chapters 6, 8, 20 and 21

Sources: S20, S16—S17, S27, S161, S162
thomasns:
Generation 3 · fishing skipper

Thomas Nielsen Silkjær

10.1.1882, Husby — 20.3.1950, Havnegade 179, Esbjerg

Where his sister Ane Johanne went inland, he went out towards the sea — to Esbjerg, the town that grew in one generation from open field to Denmark’s foremost fishing town. He has a full biography in Dansk Fiskeristat 1935—36.

Baptised
5 February 1882
Young
Confirmed in Husby in 1896 — the parish register lists him “af Økjær” and his father as “Niels Thomsen (kaldt Silkjær)”. Seaman’s book 28 September 1903; called up to the Navy, service 21.9.1905—23.4.1906. The levy roll moves him from the Husby district directly to Esbjerg with a removal certificate of 12 May 1906, and in 1910 on to the Holmsland Klit district — with a short recall to the Navy in October the same year
Married
5 May 1906 on Holmsland Klit to Kristiane Enevoldsen, b. 27.3.1873, daughter of the farmer Simon Enevoldsen of Haurvig. The witnesses were her father and her former father-in-law, the fishery warden Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen; marriage licence 30 April, probate court certificate 3 May 1906. She died on 31.7.1963 at the old people’s home in Esbjerg, buried in Gormsgade Cemetery.
Trained
The Fishing Skippers’ School in Esbjerg, 1916—17
Vessel
Master and owner of the cutter E.94 ANNE KIRSTINE, 1923—1948. Registered as “T. N. Silkjær”.
Home
Havnegade 179, Esbjerg — the bridge between the family’s two worlds
Seven children
Five with Kristiane, and the two of 1913, each with a different woman — the son Arne with his stepdaughter Kristine Oline and the daughter Else Margrethe with Nielsine Nielsen; see the sections below. The five: Kristen Lauridsen (4.5.1904 at Aargab — 31.7.1985 in Esbjerg, buried on 3 August in Gormsgade Cemetery; baptised in Haurvig Church two years before his parents’ wedding, where the parish register names Thomas as the declared father. Skipper’s examination 1924, master of E.426 BERGIT; in the tax books alternately C. L. and K. L. from 1925 to 1956) · Anna (17.2.1907 in Esbjerg — 10.10.1952 in the same place; the birthplace confirmed by the census of 1921, the dates by the Register of Deaths [S86]) · Niels (b. 26.9.1910 at Aargab, baptised in Haurvig Church) · Ejlerth Marius (b. 29.1.1915, Hjertinggade 13, baptised in Zion’s Church) · Elna Elisabeth (b. 20.1.1919) — she also appears in the census of 1930 at Gl. Færgevej 7. The family file also lists a twin sister Kirsten; the parish register has only one birth on 4 May 1904, and Kirsten is therefore treated as a duplicate.
The sons
Niels ran arms in through Esbjerg harbour with ANNE KIRSTINE in March 1945 and brought in skipper Jens Frich on VEGA; Ejlert helped Hans Kvist find more skippers. Ejlert died on 28 May 1985 and Niels on 16 April 1986; both lie in Fovrfeld Cemetery, but in separate sections. [S10, S108]
The flight, 1912
On 14 December 1912 he secretly left the home at Årgab together with the neighbours’ daughter, Nielsine Nielsen, b. 23.11.1887 — first to Kiel, where her father found them between Christmas and New Year, lodging as a married couple “from Esbjerg”; the police expelled him, and from Vamdrup they disappeared again. Then Copenhagen, where they lived together “as man and wife” — he in work at the Copenhagen Floating Dock — until he was arrested on 21 February 1913 at a quarter to seven in the morning on the corner of Strandgade and Torvegade. He declared in court that it had been his intention not to return. [S119, S129, S174, S175]
Sentenced, 1913
On 14 April 1913 the Extraordinary Court of Ulfborg-Hind Hundred sentenced him to “Eighteen Months” of hard labour in the house of correction for breach of § 162 of the Penal Code — incest with his stepdaughter Kristine Oline Enevoldsen since the summer of 1911, when she was fifteen. At the examination on 22 March he himself admitted that he “must be said to have seduced her”. The prosecutor asked for the severest penalty the law allowed, the defence for the mildest; the sentence was read to him outside the gaol on 15 April — he declared himself “satisfied” and waived his right of appeal. He began serving his sentence in Ringkjøbing Gaol on 27 April; admitted to Vridsløselille on 3 July 1913 as prisoner no. 240. His counsel, the solicitor Kamp, applied for a pardon in July with the judge’s recommendation — the Ministry of Justice refused; at the King’s jubilee on 15 November 1913 he was pardoned by royal resolution of the same day, as one of seven prisoners recommended, and released at 4 p.m. [S119, S121, S166, S167, S168]
Two children, 1913
In 1913 he appears in two parish registers as the declared father: Arne, born on 26 May at Årgab to his stepdaughter, and Else Margrethe, born on 15 November in Aarhus to Nielsine Nielsen. Arne was born while he was held in Ringkjøbing Gaol; Else Margrethe on the day he was released from Vridsløselille. [S47, S124]
Arne
The child was born on 26 May 1913 at Aargab, while he was held in Ringkjøbing Gaol, and baptised in Haurvig Church: Arne Enevoldsen. The parish register names him as “Udlagt Barnefader: Stiffader Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, 31 Aar” — declared father: stepfather Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, 31 years. In 1930 he still lives in the household at Gl. Færgevej 7 — entered as a foster child. His later life is followed in chapter 13.
Died
20 March 1950 at Havnegade 179, 68 years old; buried on 24 March in the churchyard in Gormsgade, section Ø, row 11, no. 9, with the note “D.D. (double depth)”. Kristiane was laid in the same grave on 4 August 1963. In the year of his death E.94 ANNE KIRSTINE passed to his son Niels. [S108]
Chapters
Chapters 9—13 · the sons and the cutter in chapters 17—18

Sources: S8, S9, S10, S44, S45, S46, S70, S71, S72, S73, S119, S121, S124, S166, S167, S168, S174, S175, S176
kristineoline:
Generation 3 · the stepdaughter

Kristine Oline Enevoldsen

17.5.1896, Nysogn — 18.5.1940, Esbjerg

She was born six weeks after her father, the boat skipper Christen Olesen Enevoldsen, drowned off Årgab. She never saw him. When her mother remarried in 1906, Thomas Nielsen Silkjær became her stepfather; she was nine.

Parents
Christen Olesen Enevoldsen, b. 17.10.1871 at Aargab — skipper of the boat “Forsøget”, lost in the wreck of 1.4.1896, buried from Haurvig Church on 6.4.1896 — and Christiane Enevoldsen, b. 27.3.1873
Posthumous child
She was born six weeks after the wreck and never saw her father. His name stands at the top of the memorial stone at Renderne. [S48]
Brothers and sisters
Enevold Jepsen, b. 1892, and Simon, b. 1894 — both later fishing skippers in Esbjerg
The letter
It was she herself who brought the case to light: pregnant, and without her mother’s knowledge, she wrote to Pastor Hornbech in Randers, the mission’s travelling preacher, whom she knew from his visits to the dunes — in all probability Carl Marius Hornbech, travelling preacher 1909—15, living in Randers; see caveat 31. In his reply he urged her to confide in her mother — and she did so on the Thursday evening of 13 February 1913, by handing her the letter; four days later the police constable wrote his report. [S119, S172, S174]
The case, 1911—13
The records preserve her words in reported form: before the first time, she said that it was wrong and that she might become pregnant — he brushed it aside. He admitted in court that he had seduced her. Even so, she herself was sentenced under § 162: one month’s simple imprisonment, reduced under the youth provisions §§ 21 and 37 and suspended under § 20 of the provisional Penal Code of 1 April 1911 — the court expressly gave her young age as the reason. The prosecutor had asked for the severest penalty the law allowed for her as well; the defence for a suspended sentence, and the court followed the defence. She was heavily pregnant and did not appear in court; the sentence was read to her and her guardian in person at the home at Årgab on 19 April by the parish summons officers — both declared themselves “satisfied with the Judgment”. [S119, S121, S122, S123, S174]
17 March 1913
Her own statement was taken in the home at Årgab: the court travelled out to her, because she could not come to Ringkøbing. She explained, among other things, that she knew it was wrong — but not that it was punishable; that her confidant was Anders Hejde’s eighteen-year-old son in Bjerregaard — Søren Mathiasen Heide, born on 17 November 1893; and that in December she had told her stepfather that he was to blame for her being unwell. [S163, S170]
The maintenance case
Three days after the baptism, on 18 June 1913, a paternity case was brought in her name against her stepfather — case 82/1913, “Christine Oline Enevoldsen v. Thomas Nielsen Silkjær”, concluded on 20 June. Seventeen years old, with the child’s father in gaol. [S120]
Son
Arne Enevoldsen, b. 26.5.1913 at Aargab — nine days after her seventeenth birthday. She gave birth at home at Årgab; the parish register lists her by name and age as “Ugift Moder” — unmarried mother. [S47]
After 1913
She stayed on the dunes when her mother moved to Esbjerg with the children in 1913, but by 1 February 1916 at the latest she was in the town herself: the census lists her as an unmarried domestic help at Nørregade 44 — on the same census day that Arne was listed as one of the household’s children in Hjertinggade. Married on 19.9.1916 to the fisherman Niels Peder Edvard Nielsen, from 1930 Højberg. The daughter Gerda Jensine born 23.2.1917. A household of her own at Helgolandsgade 14, first floor, in 1921 and still in 1925 — without Arne; in November 1930 at Cort Adelersgade 15b. [S75, S78, S81, S82, S133]
Died 1940
She died on 18 May 1940, at three o’clock in the night, at Esbjerg Municipal Hospital — the day after her forty-fourth birthday. The death certificate gives cancer of the uterus as the principal illness, with wasting as a complication; her home was Frodesgade 149. Buried on 22 May 1940 in Esbjerg New Cemetery — now Gormsgade Cemetery — from Zion’s parish by Pastor Birke, entered as Christine Oline Højberg née Enevoldsen. See caveat 22. [S83, S84]
Chapters
Chapters 9—13

Sources: S31, S40, S44, S45, S47, S75, S77, S78, S79, S81, S82, S83, S84, S119, S120, S121, S133, S163, S170, S174
arne:
Generation 4 · the foster child

Arne Enevoldsen

26.5.1913, Aargab — 27.12.1998, Vejle

Born six weeks after the sentence and five weeks before his father was delivered to Vridsløselille. He was given his mother’s surname and grew up in his father’s house — on paper as a foster child.

Baptised
15 June 1913 in Haurvig Church by Pastor S. R. Madsen. Godparents: the girl Johanne Andersen, smallholder Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen, smallholder Søren Andersen Jensen and smallholder Thyge Nielsen — all of Årgab
The parish register
The Nysogn parish register names them both and writes the relationship out: “Ugift Moder Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Aargab. 17 Aar. Udlagt Barnefader: Stiffader Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, 31 Aar.” — unmarried mother Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Aargab, 17 years; declared father: stepfather Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, 31 years. [S47]
The father
He was held in Ringkjøbing Gaol when Arne was born — sentenced on 14 April, admitted to Vridsløselille on 3 July. He was present neither at the birth nor at the baptism.
The maintenance
Three days after the baptism a paternity case was brought in the mother’s name against the child’s father — case 82/1913 in the district bailiff’s case list, 18—20 June 1913. The boy’s maintenance was put on a formal footing before he was a month old. [S120]
1916
The census of 1 February lists him as a two-year-old in the household at Hjertinggade 13, Esbjerg — as “Arne Silkjær”, under Children, with no distinction from Thomas and Kristiane’s own children. See caveat 21. [S76]
1930
The census of 5 November lists him as a seventeen-year-old in the household at Gl. Færgevej 7, Esbjerg, with his position in the family given as foster child — the only one in the house not called Silkjær
Married 1940
Married on 11 May 1940 in Zion’s Church by Pastor Bentzen, entered as “Ungkarl Revisor Arne Enevoldsen, Havnegade 179” — bachelor, accountant, at his father’s address — to Annagrethe Thomsen, dental technician, b. 4.4.1916 in Jerne. Witnesses: the bride’s father and “Fiskeskipper Silkjær, Havnegade 179”. The entry names only his mother. Seven days later Arne’s mother, Kristine Oline, died. [S85]
After 1940
The census of 5 November 1940 lists him on Rolfsgade in Esbjerg, and the tax books then follow him address by address in the town until 1956, when the series ends. In 1943—45 he is an accountant at Rolfsgade 127, where the family orders three photographs from Paul Bølling — a gathering in the living room and two pictures from the birth of their daughter in May 1944. By royal licence of 22 March 1954 the daughter was adopted by Annagrethe’s new husband, Ronald Søren Hyllested, and thereafter bore the name Hyllested — at her confirmation in 1959 she appears as Annette Hyllested with her mother and adoptive father at Spangsbjerg Kirkevej 42. The daughter became a nurse and moved to Copenhagen, where she lived for the rest of her life and had two children; the family does not believe she later had contact with Arne, but that cannot be established with certainty. She died in 2024, shortly after her eightieth birthday. The tax books have Arne in Esbjerg on both sides of the licence — he was alive when the adoption was granted. He died in Vejle on 27 December 1998, eighty-five years old; the death notice was placed by Edna on the family’s behalf, after the funeral had taken place. See caveats 12 and 25. [S40, S57, S86, S89, S93, S113, S147, S173]
The insurance society
The fishermen’s liability insurance society in Esbjerg had had the bank clerk E. Enevoldsen as treasurer and bookkeeper; after his death Arne took over the work. When the society was entered in the Insurance Register as no. 468 on 5 January 1945, he appears as its manager — and on the board sat, among others, the fishing skipper Thomas Silkjær. The society could be bound by the chairman together with the manager. [S140, S141]
The divorce, 1949
The marriage to Annagrethe was dissolved by licence on 3 June 1949. She was married to Ronald Søren Hyllested by the Copenhagen Magistrates on 11 February 1950. [S139]
Married 1950
Married in a civil ceremony in Esbjerg on 2 December 1950 at 12.10 to the telephonist Edna Alice Söderwall, née Gram, b. 21.9.1913 in Esbjerg. Both divorced; both residing at Strandbygade 39. The witnesses were two office workers; no family members stood as witnesses. At her death in Vejle in 2002 Edna still bore the name Enevoldsen. [S40, S139]
Chapters
Chapters 11—13

Sources: S40, S44, S45, S46, S47, S76, S85, S86, S89, S93, S120, S139, S140, S141
anejohanne:
Generation 3 · the direct line

Ane Johanne

22.10.1883, Økjær — 19.11.1956

The most important woman in the story, and the one the sources say least about. She did not marry into a landscape but into a trade — and became the first in the direct line to leave the coast altogether.

Baptised
18 November 1883, Husby Church
Married
22 March 1906, Husby Church, to Mads Erik Madsen (b. 28.7.1879 at Øster Finderup in Hanning parish, baptised in Hanning Church 17.8.1879 — d. 2.8.1951), bricklayer and later master mason
Moved
Husby (census 1890) → Sædding near Rækker Mølle (1911, 1916, 1921, 1925) → Vorgod (1930), where she died
Fourteen children
Anne 1907 · Knud 1908 · Niels Silkjær 1909 · Alma 1910 · Kristine 1911 · Erik 1912 · Dagmar 1913 · Georg 1914 · Ninna 1915 · Laura 1917 · Ellen Marie 1918 · Signe 1922 · Christian 1923 · Elisabeth 1925 — eighteen years between the eldest and the youngest
Her voice
Her son’s name. Someone set the mother’s family name in the middle of the name of a child born forty kilometres from the farm, in a parish where the name meant nothing to anyone else.
Chapters
Chapters 14—16 · childhood in chapter 8, mentioned in 19—21

Sources: S5, S6, S7, S21
jensclaus:
Generation 3 · the Vejlby branch

Jens Klaus Nielsen Silkjær

6.5.1886, Økjær — 25.7.1959, Allingåbro

He left the west coast and became gravedigger and verger at Vejlby Church on Djursland. With him Silkjær became a fixed, inherited surname in a quite different part of Jutland.

Born
6 May 1886. Both censuses (1925 and 1930) give 06.05.1886; the year 1880 given in one archive is an error. The birthplace appears as “Ringkøbing” in the censuses, where the family’s records say Husby — probably the county used as the birthplace.
Spring 1911
Wrote home on 18 April from Øster Alling Præstegaard to his sister Kirstine at Husby Præstegaard — with his sweetheart and a weekend visit home in prospect. [S130]
Married
28 October 1911 in Fausing to Bodil Marie Bossow, b. 8 April 1887 in Auning
Occupation
Verger and gravedigger at Vejlby Church, Allingåbro
Home
Øster Alling → Nimtofte by 1921 → Vejlby (Vejlbyvej 2) by 1925. Whether Vejlbyvej 2 was the gravedigger’s house has not been established.
Six sons
Johannes 1912 · Niels 1914 · Henry Johan 1915—1989 · Tage Ewald 1917 (all born at Oustrup, Øster Alling) · Oluf Kristian 1920—2005 · Verner 1921 (Nimtofte)
The name
Silkjær as a fixed surname — his son is described as the “son of gravedigger and verger Jens Silkjær in Allingåbro”
Died
25 July 1959 in Allingåbro, 73 years old. His wife Bodil Marie outlived him by almost ten years. [S40]
Chapters
Chapters 8 and 19 · the branches in chapter 20

Sources: S18, S34, S35, S36, S130
bodilmarie:
Generation 3 · the Vejlby branch

Bodil Marie Bossow

8.4.1887, Auning — 13.7.1969

She is the woman the censuses could not spell. Two forms, two names — and the same date of birth both times.

Married
28 October 1911 in Fausing to Jens Klaus Nielsen Silkjær
Census 1925
Entered as “Bodil Alycia Silkjær”
Census 1930

kristiane:
Generation 3 · the widow from Årgab

Kristiane Enevoldsen

27.3.1873, Haurvig — 31.7.1963, Esbjerg

Married at 19, widowed at 23, married again at 33 to a man almost nine years younger than she was. She lived to 90 and died in Esbjerg, a hundred kilometres from the dunes where she was born.

Parents
Farmer Simon Enevoldsen and Ane Marie Christensen, Haurvig
Married 1)
1 April 1892 in Haurvig Church to Christen Olesen Enevoldsen, b. 17.10.1871 at Årgab, smallholder, fisherman and boat skipper — the same surname, but two different Enevoldsen families on the dunes
Widow
He drowned off Årgab beach on 1 April 1896 — exactly four years after the wedding. The body was found the next day on Peder Christian Nielsen’s (Dahl) stretch of beach at Bjerregaard and buried from Haurvig Church on 6 April, Easter Monday.
Sons
Enevold Jepsen, b. 13 October 1892, named after his paternal grandfather — and Simon, b. 2 May 1894, named after his maternal grandfather.
Married 2)
5 May 1906 in Haurvig Church to the fisherman Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, b. 1882 — the witnesses were her father and her former father-in-law. The son Kristen had been born two years before the wedding, in 1904; the parish register named Thomas as the declared father.
The widow’s years
She lived as a widow for ten years with three children, “entirely without Means”, and received support from the Harboøre Fund — the fund from the disaster of 1893. Of her second marriage she said in court that it had not been entered into for the sake of support but was founded on “a strong and deep Love”. [S119]
In court, 1913
Her statement of 7 March 1913 is the longest in the case: how her daughter handed her Hornbech’s letter, the marriage, the suspicion about Nielsine, which he denied. She did not wish charges to be brought against him for adultery — and the same day reached a settlement in the maintenance case: 300 kroner a year for her and 90 kroner for each of the three children of the marriage. When the court sat in the home at Årgab on 17 March to examine her daughter, she was in all probability herself one of the two court witnesses — the signature “Chr. Silkær”; see caveat 29. At the final hearing on 26 March she and the guardian withdrew charges under § 174. [S119, S163]
Died
31 July 1963 in Esbjerg, 90 years old
Caveat
The sons’ birth entries have not been read in the original in Nysogn (Haurvig church district), births 1892—1894. The number of three children is confirmed by the prison register’s “3 Stedbørn” — three stepchildren. [S31, S32, S44, S45]

Esper

17.3.1888, Økjær — 1.12.1960

The brother who took the name inland. Esper became a farmer and millwright, married into Gudum and had eight children on the farm Nørre Tangshus — one of them carried the trade on as a millstone dresser, and the youngest took the name all the way to Australia.

Born
17 March 1888 in Økjær, Husby parish — baptised on 29 March in Husby Church
Occupation
Farmer and millwright, later farm owner
Married
17 March 1913 — his twenty-fifth birthday — in Gudum to Jensine Mortensen, b. 9 July 1889 at Nørre Tangshus in Gudum parish, daughter of Jens Mortensen and Kristiane Knudsen — d. 10 December 1982 in Struer, 93 years old
The farm
The couple set up home on the farm where she was born, Nørre Tangshus in Gudum; in their old age they moved to a house at Fredensgade 11 in Struer
Children
Eight children, all born at Nørre Tangshus: Knud Vognsgaard (1913—1959, smelter, killed in the explosion at the steelworks in Frederiksværk — see chapter 20), Niels (1914—1999, farmer in Gudum, eight children), Jens (1916—2000, farmer, millstone dresser and parish council chairman, nine children), Anne Kristiane (1917—2009, twelve children on a farm in Hjerm — it was she who, as “Ane Pedersen, née Silkjær”, wrote the obituary of her brother), Krista (1920—2006), Alma (1923—2013, lived and died on Ærø), Helga (1925—2004) and Otto (b. 1932, emigrated to Australia)
Grief, 1959
A year and a half before his own death, Esper lost his eldest son: Knud was killed on 27 May 1959 in the great explosion at the steelworks in Frederiksværk, one of five workers who lost their lives that day. The family from Skævinge had visited Fredensgade at Easter [S148, S149, S150]
Died
1 December 1960 in Struer

Karen Marie

1.3.1890, Økjær — 3.3.1933

Sister of both Ane Johanne and the Esbjerg skipper Thomas. She died at 43, two days after her birthday, and was buried on 9 March 1933. She too passed the family name on in the middle of her son’s name.

Smallholder’s wife in Sjælborg

18 September 1913 in Husby Church to Kristian Kornelius Bøndergaard, b. 18 May 1888 in Esbjerg

Kristian Kornelius was born in Esbjerg in 1888 — twenty years after the town was founded, in the very first generation of Esbjerg-born. The marriage is one more thread between Husby and the harbour town, alongside her brother Thomas’ move.

jensine:
Generation 3 · Fjand

Jensine Kristine

17.12.1896, Økjær — 23.2.1964, Fjand

She stayed by the coast. From Økjær she went only one parish north, to Fjand in Sønder Nissum, and there she lived for the rest of her life — twenty-eight of those years as a widow.

Born
17 December 1896 in Økjær, Husby parish
The son, 1917
On 28 April 1917 she gave birth in Økjær to a son, Niels Poulsen, at twenty and unmarried; the declared father was the farmhand Laurits Nikolaj Poulsen, 22, of Gudum. The boy was baptised on Whit Sunday, 27 May, in Husby Church, carried by her sister Ane Kirstine and with her father Niels Silkjær among the godparents. The child’s father died unmarried on 28 November 1923 at the county hospital in Lemvig, 28 years old — the boy was six. In the census of 1925 he is with his grandparents at Peder Skramsgade 2 in Esbjerg as a foster son; in November 1930 he is with her in Fjand, together with Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand and his half-brother Evald [S96, S105, S106, S115]
Married
Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand, b. 10 August 1894 in Sønder Nissum — d. 9 February 1936, 41 years old
With Martin
Three children: Jeppe Kristian, Evald and Anne Marie Jeppesen Nørfjand. Evald was born on 10 November 1927 at half past nine at Pilgaardhus, Sønder Nissum parish, and baptised in the church on Boxing Day; his mother carried the child herself, and among the godparents stood two bachelors named Jeppesen Nørfjand, probably the father’s brothers. The entry lists her as wife — so the marriage took place in 1927 at the latest. Jeppe Kristian and Anne Marie follow the family’s own records [S40, S106, S107]
Died
23 February 1964 in Fjand, Sønder Nissum parish

Sidsel Kathrine

24.12.1894, Økjær — 18.5.1938, Esbjerg

The Christmas Eve child from Økjær became the one of the sisters who had a profession. A nurse in Esbjerg, a household of her own in Læborg — unmarried all her life, dead of pulmonary tuberculosis at forty-three.

Born
Christmas Eve, 24 December 1894, in Økjær, Husby parish — number seven of the children
The profession
Nurse. Esbjerg’s tax book for 1927 lists her as head nurse at Gl. Færgevej 7 — the same address as her brother Thomas [S145]
Læborg
On 1 December 1927 she moved from Esbjerg to Læborg, lodging with a haulier. At the census of November 1930 she is still living there — but no longer as a lodger: by then she has her own household [S145, S146]
Havnegade
When she returned to Esbjerg the sources do not say. At her death she lived at Havnegade 152 — the same street as her brother Thomas at no. 179 and her brother-in-law Christen Torbensen at no. 132 [S108, S142]
Died
18 May 1938 at 6 p.m. at her home, of pulmonary tuberculosis, forty-three years old and unmarried; the death certificate lists her as a former nurse. Buried on 26 May in the churchyard in Gormsgade — twelve years before her brother Thomas was laid there [S142]
